expected_facts.statement: The concept note is addressed to the Green Climate Fund Simplified Approval Process.
The Office of Climate Resilience leads delivery together with the Department of Public Works.
The measures are delivered between 2027 and 2032.
Harbor Point recorded 23 days above 35 °C in 2025, against a 1991-2020 average of 9 days per year.
Street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event.
The project plants 4,800 street trees along 12 cool corridors in Eastside and Millbrook.
The project builds 85 bioretention cells and converts 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards into permeable green play areas.
The tree canopy target for Eastside and Millbrook is 25 percent by 2032.
The programme costs USD 26.5 million; the city contributes USD 7.9 million from its capital budget and USD 18.6 million in external grant funding is sought, not secured.

Cool corridor planting and three years of establishment watering are estimated at USD 9.6 million and green stormwater infrastructure at USD 14.2 million; the USD 2.7 million cooling network is funded from the city operating budget.
Public Works delivers green stormwater infrastructure, the Unified School District hosts schoolyard conversions, and Millbrook Neighbours Alliance co-designs cool corridor routes.
The Office of Climate Resilience publishes an annual progress report tracking canopy cover, flooded intersections and heat-related emergency visits.

## Project summary

### Project title and location

**Project title:** Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan  
**City:** Harbor Point  
[Information needed: Confirm the country in which Harbor Point is located.]

### Project duration and scope

The Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan will reduce extreme-heat exposure and street flooding between 2027 and 2032. Harbor Point has 182,400 residents.

### Implementing entities

The Office of Climate Resilience leads delivery together with the Department of Public Works. The Department of Public Works delivers green stormwater infrastructure. The Harbor Point Unified School District hosts schoolyard conversions, and Millbrook Neighbours Alliance co-designs cool corridor routes with residents.

[Information needed: Confirm the accredited entity for the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan's GCF SAP funding proposal.]

### Financing

The total programme cost is USD 26.5 million. Harbor Point will contribute USD 7.9 million from its capital budget. The plan seeks USD 18.6 million in external grant funding.

[Information needed: Confirm the amount requested from the Green Climate Fund for the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

## Climate rationale and baseline

### Extreme heat

Harbor Point recorded 23 days above 35 °C in 2025, compared with an average of 9 such days per year between 1991 and 2020. Heat-related emergency department visits rose from 140 in 2021 to 310 in 2025.

Eastside and Millbrook have the city’s lowest tree canopy, at 11 percent and 13 percent respectively. Harbor Point has 182,400 residents.

[Information needed: Confirm the number of Harbor Point residents exposed to extreme heat.]

[Information needed: Provide the documented without-project baseline for extreme-heat exposure in Harbor Point.]

### Stormwater flooding

Street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event. The Canal Street underpass closed six times in 2025 because of standing water. The existing drainage network in Eastside was designed for a 5-year storm and is undersized for current rainfall intensities.

The Canal Street underpass and the Eastside drainage network are identified as assets affected by current stormwater conditions.

[Information needed: Confirm the number of Harbor Point residents exposed to stormwater flooding.]

[Information needed: Provide the documented without-project baseline for stormwater flooding in Harbor Point.]

## Project components and activities

### Component 1: Cool corridors

The plan will plant 4,800 street trees along 12 cool corridors connecting schools, clinics, and transit stops in Eastside and Millbrook. The target is to increase tree canopy cover in both neighbourhoods to 25 percent by 2032. Cool corridor planting includes three years of establishment watering and is estimated to cost USD 9.6 million.

Millbrook Neighbours Alliance will co-design cool corridor routes with residents.

### Component 2: Green stormwater infrastructure

The plan will build 85 bioretention cells and convert 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards into permeable green play areas. Together, these measures are designed to capture the first 25 millimetres of rainfall from 41 hectares of impervious surface. Green stormwater infrastructure, including design and construction supervision, is estimated to cost USD 14.2 million.

The Department of Public Works delivers green stormwater infrastructure. The Harbor Point Unified School District hosts schoolyard conversions.

[Information needed: Confirm the locations of the 85 bioretention cells planned under the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

[Information needed: Confirm the schoolyard sites included in the 3.2-hectare permeable green play-area conversions under the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

### Component 3: Community cooling network

The Office of Climate Resilience will designate 18 community cooling centres in libraries and recreation centres, with extended opening hours on days above 32 °C. The community cooling network is funded from the city operating budget at USD 2.7 million.

[Information needed: Confirm the locations of the 18 community cooling centres under the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

## Expected results and indicators

### Expected adaptation results

The Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan sets out to reduce extreme-heat exposure and street flooding between 2027 and 2032. The proposed cool corridors will plant 4,800 street trees along 12 corridors connecting schools, clinics, and transit stops in Eastside and Millbrook, with a tree canopy target of 25 percent in both neighbourhoods by 2032.

The proposed green stormwater infrastructure includes 85 bioretention cells and 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards converted into permeable green play areas. Together, these measures are designed to capture the first 25 millimetres of rainfall from 41 hectares of impervious surface. The community cooling network will designate 18 cooling centres in libraries and recreation centres, with extended opening hours on days above 32 °C.

[Information needed: Confirm the number of direct beneficiaries of the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

[Information needed: Confirm the beneficiary groups for the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

### Indicators, baselines and targets

| Indicator | Baseline | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tree canopy cover in Eastside | 11 percent | 25 percent by 2032 |
| Tree canopy cover in Millbrook | 13 percent | 25 percent by 2032 |
| Number of flooded intersections during monitored storms | Street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event. | [Information needed: Confirm the target number of flooded intersections during monitored storms for the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.] |
| Heat-related emergency department visits | 310 visits in 2025 | [Information needed: Confirm the target for heat-related emergency department visits under the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.] |

### Monitoring and reporting

The Office of Climate Resilience will publish an annual progress report. The reported indicators include tree canopy cover, the number of flooded intersections during monitored storms, and heat-related emergency department visits.

## Implementation arrangements

### Lead and delivery entities

The Office of Climate Resilience leads delivery together with the Department of Public Works. The Office of Climate Resilience will designate 18 community cooling centres in libraries and recreation centres, with extended opening hours on days above 32 °C. The Department of Public Works delivers green stormwater infrastructure.

[Information needed: Confirm the entity that will serve as the accredited entity for the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan's GCF SAP funding proposal.]

### Delivery partners

The Harbor Point Unified School District hosts schoolyard conversions. Millbrook Neighbours Alliance co-designs cool corridor routes with residents.

### Governance

The Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan was adopted by the Harbor Point City Council on 14 March 2026.

[Information needed: Confirm the governance arrangement for implementation of the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

### Monitoring and reporting

The Office of Climate Resilience will publish an annual progress report. Indicators include tree canopy cover, the number of flooded intersections during monitored storms, and heat-related emergency department visits.

## Indicative financing

### Total programme cost and cost basis

The total programme cost is USD 26.5 million for implementation between 2027 and 2032. Component costs are based on the estimates in the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan: cool corridor planting includes three years of establishment watering, and green stormwater infrastructure includes design and construction supervision.

| Component | Indicative cost (USD million) | Funding status |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Cool corridors | 9.6 | Seeking grant funding |
| Green stormwater infrastructure | 14.2 | Seeking grant funding |
| Community cooling network | 2.7 | Funded from the city operating budget |
| **Total programme cost** | **26.5** |  |

### Co-financing

Harbor Point will contribute USD 7.9 million from its capital budget. The community cooling network is funded from the city operating budget at USD 2.7 million.

### Green Climate Fund request

The plan seeks USD 18.6 million in external grant funding.

[Information needed: Confirm the amount requested from the Green Climate Fund for the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

[Information needed: Confirm the financial instrument requested from the Green Climate Fund for the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]
